hypothesis: The measured 128-thread tile was faster than the 192-, 256-, and 512-thread tiles. A 96-thread CTA with a matching 96-source tile uses 2,688 bytes of shared memory and three warps; its smaller footprint may help resource use, while more tile iterations and barriers may offset that benefit. Measure this tradeoff without assuming a speedup.
notes: The existing kernel derives the tile length and source loading from blockDim.x, so changing the launch values preserves one target per thread, partial-tile handling, output bounds, and the existing barrier pattern.
